subject: Biology
title: Evolution
summary: Life probably arose about 4 billion years ago from non-living organic molecules (chemical evolution — Oparin and Haldane; Miller's experiment). The universe is about 20 billion years old; Earth about 4.5 billion years.

Evidence for evolution: palaeontology (fossils), comparative anatomy (homologous and analogous organs), molecular similarities and observed natural selection (industrial melanism, antibiotic resistance).

Darwin's theory: variation, overproduction, struggle for existence, natural selection (survival of the fittest — fitness means reproductive fitness). De Vries added mutation (saltation). The Hardy–Weinberg principle describes a population that is not evolving.
Adaptive radiation (Darwin's finches, Australian marsupials) and human evolution from Dryopithecus to Homo sapiens complete the chapter.

formulas.name: Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium
formulas.formula: p + q = 1;  p² + 2pq + q² = 1  (p, q = allele frequencies; p² and q² homozygotes, 2pq heterozygotes)
formulas.when: Testing whether a population is evolving.

formulas.name: Factors disturbing H–W equilibrium
formulas.formula: gene migration (gene flow), genetic drift (founder effect), mutation, genetic recombination, natural selection

formulas.name: Types of natural selection
formulas.formula: stabilising (average favoured, peak gets taller);  directional (one extreme favoured, peak shifts);  disruptive (both extremes favoured, two peaks)

formulas.name: Miller's experiment (1953)
formulas.formula: CH₄ + NH₃ + H₂ + water vapour, electric discharge at 800 °C → amino acids

formulas.name: Homologous organs
formulas.formula: same structure/origin, different functions → divergent evolution;  forelimbs of whale, bat, cheetah, human;  heart and brain of vertebrates;  thorn of Bougainvillea and tendril of Cucurbita

formulas.name: Analogous organs
formulas.formula: different structure, same function → convergent evolution;  wings of butterfly and bird;  eyes of Octopus and mammals;  flippers of penguins and dolphins;  sweet potato (root) and potato (stem)

formulas.name: Industrial melanism
formulas.formula: England, peppered moth (Biston betularia): before industrialisation more white moths; after (soot-darkened trees, no lichens) more dark moths

formulas.name: Adaptive radiation
formulas.formula: Darwin's finches (Galapagos — different beaks for diet);  Australian marsupials radiating from one ancestor;  placental mammals parallel them (convergent evolution)
formulas.when: Many forms from one ancestor in an area.

formulas.name: Lamarck vs Darwin
formulas.formula: Lamarck: use and disuse of organs, inheritance of acquired characters (giraffe neck);  Darwin: branching descent and natural selection;  de Vries: mutations, saltation (single-step large mutation) in Oenothera

formulas.name: Geological timeline (plants)
formulas.formula: seaweeds and a few plants ~320 mya (mya = million years ago);  seed ferns → gymnosperms → angiosperms

formulas.name: Animal timeline
formulas.formula: jawless fish ~350 mya;  lobefins (coelacanth) → first amphibians;  fish-like reptiles (Ichthyosaurs) ~200 mya;  dinosaurs disappeared ~65 mya;  first mammals shrew-like

formulas.name: Human evolution
formulas.formula: Dryopithecus and Ramapithecus (~15 mya) → Australopithecines (~2 mya, East Africa) → Homo habilis (650–800 cc, no meat) → Homo erectus (~1.5 mya, 900 cc, ate meat) → Neanderthal man (1400 cc, buried dead, 1,00,000–40,000 years ago) → Homo sapiens (arose in Africa; ice age 75,000–10,000 years ago)

examples.title: Heterozygote frequency
examples.problem: In a population, the recessive allele frequency q = 0.3. Frequency of heterozygotes?

examples.title: Homologous or analogous?
examples.problem: Bougainvillea thorns and Cucurbita tendrils — homologous or analogous?
examples.solution: Homologous: both are modified stems (axillary structures), showing divergent evolution.

examples.title: Antibiotic resistance
examples.problem: How is antibiotic resistance an example of evolution?
examples.solution: Bacteria with resistance-giving mutations survive antibiotic treatment and multiply; the population changes over a short time scale — natural selection.

examples.title: Founder effect
examples.solution: When a small group separates and founds a new population, its allele frequencies may differ greatly by chance (genetic drift); the original drifted population becomes the founders.

examples.title: Brain capacity
examples.problem: Arrange by brain capacity: Homo erectus, Homo habilis, Neanderthal man.
examples.solution: Homo habilis (650–800 cc) < Homo erectus (~900 cc) < Neanderthal man (~1400 cc).

examples.title: Fitness in Darwin's sense
examples.problem: What does 'fitness' mean in natural selection?
examples.solution: Reproductive fitness — those better fit in an environment leave more progeny; it is not about physical strength.

topics.title: Origin of life
topics.explain: The Big Bang theory explains the origin of the universe. Early Earth had no atmosphere; water vapour, methane, CO₂ and ammonia were released from molten mass; UV rays split water. Life appeared about 500 million years after Earth formed. Spontaneous generation was disproved by Louis Pasteur; panspermia proposes spores came from outer space.

topics.title: Theory of special creation vs evolution
topics.explain: Special creation held that all species were created as they are, Earth is about 4000 years old and diversity has always been the same — challenged by fossils and studies showing Earth is about 4.5 billion years old.

topics.title: Fossils and dating
topics.explain: Fossils are remains of hard parts of life forms in rocks; different-aged rock layers show different life forms. Their age is found by radioactive dating.

topics.title: Embryological evidence
topics.explain: Proposed by Ernst Haeckel: all vertebrate embryos have a row of vestigial gill slits behind the head. Karl Ernst von Baer disproved the idea that embryos pass through adult stages of other animals.

topics.title: Mechanism of evolution
topics.explain: Variation arises from mutation, recombination during gametogenesis, and gene flow or genetic drift. Natural selection acts on this variation; over generations, new species can arise (speciation).

topics.title: Brief account of evolution
topics.explain: Around 2000 mya the first cellular forms appeared; single cells became multicellular; invertebrates formed and became active by 500 mya. Fish with stout fins could move onto land (coelacanth, 1938 South Africa). Amphibians evolved into reptiles with thick-shelled eggs.
